description: Improving Pollinator Habitat on McConnell Air Force Base is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Military base managers have traditionally used non-native plant species in their landscaping. These non-native species provide limited food and habitat for native pollinators. Moreover, even though the AFB is located along a key migratory pathway for monarch butterflies, and contains important local natural resources, building a pollinator-friendly landscape had previously not been a priority. Coverage: Wichita, KS (2021). The toolkit gives Wichita, KS as the location, 2021 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
